questions.question: When hexane boils, what is actually overcome?
options: The covalent bonds inside each molecule
The intermolecular forces between the molecules
Both the covalent bonds and the intermolecular forces

questions.question: The only intermolecular force acting between nonpolar alkane molecules is:
Hydrogen bonding between molecules occurs when hydrogen is bonded directly to:
For equal chain length, the ranking of families from weakest to strongest intermolecular forces is:
Boiling points rise from ethane to decane because longer chains have:
options: Larger surfaces and more electrons, so stronger London forces

questions.question: Hexane boils at 68,7 °C but its isomer 2,2-dimethylbutane boils at 49,7 °C. The branched isomer boils lower because it:
options: Has a compact shape with less surface contact, weakening the dispersion forces

questions.question: Which of these C₆H₁₄ isomers has the HIGHEST boiling point?
options: They are equal, since the formula is the same

questions.question: As intermolecular forces get stronger, boiling point and vapour pressure respectively:
Pentane (M = 72 g·mol⁻¹) boils at 36,1 °C while butan-1-ol (M = 74 g·mol⁻¹) boils at 117,7 °C. The main reason is that butan-1-ol:
options: Forms hydrogen bonds between its molecules

questions.question: Butanal boils higher than pentane of nearly equal molar mass because aldehydes have:
options: Dipole-dipole forces in addition to London forces

questions.question: Butanoic acid boils far higher than alcohols of similar size because its molecules:
options: Hydrogen-bond at two sites, forming pairs clamped by a double hydrogen bond
Have no London forces to weaken them

questions.question: Short alcohols dissolve in water while alkanes do not, because alcohols:
options: Can hydrogen-bond with the water molecules

subtopics.title: Vapour Pressure and the Four-Step Answer

questions.question: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by:
options: The atmosphere pressing on a liquid's surface
The vapour of a liquid in equilibrium with the liquid, in a closed container
Any gas confined in a syringe
A boiling liquid on its container walls

questions.question: A volatile liquid is one with:
options: Weak intermolecular forces and a high vapour pressure
Strong intermolecular forces and a low vapour pressure

questions.question: A liquid boils at the temperature where:
options: Its vapour pressure equals the surrounding atmospheric pressure

questions.question: The final step of the four-step explanation must link stronger intermolecular forces to:
options: More energy needed to overcome them

questions.question: In the velcro picture, a longer carbon chain means:
options: A longer strip of velcro — more grip and a higher boiling point

questions.question: Branching lowers the boiling point because a branched molecule behaves like:
options: A strip of velcro with extra hooks
A crumpled ball of velcro that touches its neighbours only in small patches
A magnet that lost its pull

questions.question: When a liquid boils, what actually tears apart?
options: The hydrogen atoms from the carbons
The grip between molecules — each molecule leaves intact
The functional groups from the chains

questions.question: The "fridge magnets" carried by aldehydes and ketones represent:
options: Dipole-dipole attraction between their polar molecules

questions.question: The strongest grip in the syllabus — the "handshake" — needs a hydrogen bonded directly to:
options: An oxygen, as in an alcohol's OH group

questions.question: Butanoic acid tops the boiling-point chart because its molecules:
options: Are the heaviest in the topic
Pair up, clasped together by two hydrogen bonds

questions.question: Petrol will not mix with water because its molecules offer water:
options: Only London forces, which cannot compete with water's hydrogen-bond network

questions.question: Nail polish remover empties itself from an open bottle because its molecules:
options: Grip each other weakly, so many escape — a high vapour pressure

questions.question: Strong intermolecular forces give a liquid:
options: A low vapour pressure and a high boiling point
A high vapour pressure and a high boiling point
A low vapour pressure and a low boiling point
A high vapour pressure and a low boiling point

questions.question: You can smell an ester across a room because esters:
options: Are volatile enough for many molecules to escape into the air

questions.question: The four-step explanation for any boiling point or vapour pressure difference runs:
options: Structural difference, forces named, strengths compared, energy linked
